title: Hateful lines stay on the page
statement: Keep a studied text's slurs and hateful lines on the page only, never voiced, staged or lit, and skip whole sentences so no fragment of one is performed.
example: One audio build skips 4 listed ranges of racist lines and aborts if any other voiced line matches its slur pattern.
detail: A 3D version of the Grade 9 lessons keeps the play's racist lines as text only, never voiced, staged or lit (`othello-archive/README.md`, line 84). Its audio build skips listed ranges, which may cover a whole sentence so no fragment is performed, and aborts the run if any unlisted voiced line matches a slur pattern (`othello-archive/scripts/play_audio.py`, lines 65-73). The stage-move gate fails a move on one of those lines, and the audio check fails a clip in which a word from a skipped line can be heard (`othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, line 6; `othello-archive/scripts/play_audio_check.py`, line 9).
against: The lines stay readable and quotable: a learner may quote such language in writing, and the marker treats it as the speaker's weapon, matter-of-factly (`othello-archive/server/tasks/practice.mjs`, line 46); a draft checkpoint quotes one in its question (`othello-archive/src/content/checks.ts`, line 26); and the course names the language plainly as the characters' prejudice, never playing it for drama (`othello-archive/BRIEF.md`, line 43).

evidence.quote: Racist lines in the play are text only. They are never voiced, staged or lit.
A range may cover a whole sentence so no fragment of it is performed.
Belt and braces: any unlisted voiced line matching this aborts the run.
the move's line is one of the never-staged racist lines (play_audio.py SKIP)
and no word from the skipped racist lines may be heard
